aarch64-cuda.notes: UNMEASURED — derived from upstream guidance, not benchmarked. No HomeBrain box with this platform tag exists yet; treat every number here as a starting point, not a result. Rationale for each departure from the x86_64-vulkan flags: no -ot (128 GB unified holds the whole model, so nothing goes to CPU — the offload regex exists only because 16 GB cannot), -ngl 999 (same reason), full 131072 context (the 81920 cap is a VRAM-eviction ceiling that does not apply), --no-mmap (effectively mandatory on unified memory), -ub 2048 (upstream DGX Spark tuning), --threads 10 (the 10 Cortex-X925 performance cores, not all 20). min_healthy_vram_mb is deliberately not restated and so inherits 15000 from the model, which is inert here — verify_llama_allocation skips the watermark entirely on unified memory, which is the single place that guard belongs. Benchmark before trusting.

benchmark.measured_on: AMD RX 9060 XT, AMD Ryzen 5 5600 6-core, Vulkan + RADV_PERFTEST=rm_kq=1, llama.cpp b10107, q8 KV, -ub 2048, -ot blk.20-39, ctx 81920, whisper on CPU
benchmark.notes: DEFAULT (2026-07-25). Moved from -ub 4096/b9381 to -ub 2048/b10107 after the shipped ub4096 config was measured EVICTING 1-in-2 on the pinned build itself (guarded, single-server, drained: 28.7 t/s sustained on a good run vs 22.2 t/s and VRAM -477 MiB on a bad one, from a byte-identical starting allocation). -ub 2048 is deterministic instead: two runs produced identical idle (15197) and identical post-fill (15230) VRAM, 2/2 PASS on b10107, 3/3 on b9381. Net vs the old default's GOOD runs: sustained TG 28.7 -> 29.0, headroom 898 -> 1107 MiB, deep-fill PP 565 -> 625, and the 50%% eviction risk removed. The one cost is shallow-prompt PP@2k 758 -> 618 (-19%%); the micro-batch is what sizes the compute buffer, and that buffer relocating to GTT mid-fill was the whole failure. For maximum margin (headroom 2231) use -ot blk.18-39 with -ub 2048 at ~-4%% TG. See docs/BENCHMARKS.md (2026-07-25). Superseded as the catalog default by Muse-Glimmer-30B-UD-Q4_K_XL (2026-08-14).

benchmark.measured_on: AMD RX 9060 XT, AMD Ryzen 5 5600 6-core, Vulkan + RADV_PERFTEST=rm_kq=1, llama.cpp b10361, q4_0 KV, -ub 1024, ctx 81920, whisper on CPU
benchmark.notes: Unsloth Dynamic V3 UD-IQ4_XS as of 2026-08-19 (14,252,845,984 bytes / 13,592 MiB). The IQ4_XS file it replaces 404s. Same flags and 81920 ctx; ~1.4 GB smaller so min_healthy_vram_mb is 14000 (the IQ4_XS 15700 minus the file-size drop), unmeasured. TG/PP below are the 2026-08-14 IQ4_XS numbers. Supersedes Qwen3.6-27B-IQ4_XS (2026-08-14). Same `qwen35` Gated-DeltaNet hybrid, so the DeltaNet rules carry over unchanged: -ngl 99, no -ot, no nkvo (partial offload / nkvo break the fused kernel), and -fa with explicit ctk/ctv is mandatory on AMD Vulkan. 64 layers, only 16 full-attention (full_attention_interval 4) but those carry a FAT cache -- 4 KV heads x 256 head_dim x 2 x 16 = 32768 values/token, i.e. 18 KiB/token at q4_0 and 34 KiB/token at q8_0. That is why KV type is the context lever: q8_0 was measured at +512 MiB over q4_0 at ctx 32768 (the theoretical delta to the byte) and caps the model between 32K and 49K, roughly HALF the q4_0 ceiling -- q4_0 is what makes 81920 reachable. ctx 81920 is the eviction-gate maximum: VRAM pinned at 16110 MiB (194 MiB headroom) across a 72849-token fill with TG 17.15 -> 17.14 and byte-stable VRAM. Above it degrades rather than crashing, because the driver spills to GTT instead of failing: 98304 -> 12.6 t/s, 114688 -> 11.41 t/s with PP 70.8, 131072 dies on the first request. Shallow probes do NOT detect this -- a 200-token completion never touches the deep cache and reports full speed well past the point the cache stops fitting. Oddity: ctx 65536 specifically runs at 14.91 t/s (-13%) while both 57344 and 73728 hold 17.17; the Qwen3.6-27B measured 14.93 at 64K on this same card, so the dip is reproducible and value-specific, not a monotonic ceiling. -ub 1024 sizes the compute buffer and is the pick: -ub 512 frees 359 MiB but costs 26% TG and 77% PP. THROUGHPUT ALTERNATIVE: this GGUF carries its MTP block (blk.64.nextn.*, reported 'unused -- ignoring' until --spec-type draft-mtp is passed). Enabling it costs ~684 MiB and yields 30.4 t/s (+76%) at 68% draft acceptance, but only below ~49152 -- at ctx 81920 headroom falls to 62 MiB and PP collapses 438 -> 91. ctx 40960 + '--spec-type draft-mtp --spec-draft-n-max 2' is the max-throughput point (30.42 t/s, 276 MiB headroom). Max context was chosen over max throughput here. Vision is NOT available: the image encoder ships as a separate mmproj-*.gguf that this entry does not load, so no vision tensors are resident at all. Reasoning effort: this template takes `reasoning_effort` (xhigh/medium/low) -- NOT Muse Glimmer's `reasoning_strength`, which it would silently ignore -- and already defaults to xhigh, so the kwarg pins the shipped behaviour rather than changing it. Unlike the 35B-A3B this entry carries no --reasoning-budget, so nothing caps think tokens server-side; that is why its max_tokens is 12288 rather than the 8192 measured on Glimmer. See docs/BENCHMARKS.md (2026-08-14).

benchmark.measured_on: AMD RX 9060 XT, AMD Ryzen 5 5600 6-core, Vulkan + RADV_PERFTEST=rm_kq=1, llama.cpp master 689e227, q8_0 KV, -ub 1024, ctx 131072, whisper on CPU
benchmark.notes: DEFAULT (2026-08-14). Selectable as of the b10361 pin. muse-glimmer support merged upstream 2026-08-10 (PR #26841) and first reached a release tag on 2026-08-11 (b10356+); the earlier b10107 pin could not load this file at all. b10361 was measured against the master build it was validated on and is identical: idle 15968 vs 15969 MiB, TG 18.79 vs 18.83, PP 480.0 vs 479.5. Dense 30B + 1.8B ViT perception encoder. The whole 131072 window fits in 16 GB because the KV is unusually cheap: 52 layers of which only 13 are full-attention (the rest sliding-window 2048) and GQA with 2 KV heads. -ub 1024 is the lever that matters -- it sizes the compute buffer, and -ub 2048 costs ~460 MiB more for the same throughput. Headroom is 335 MiB idle / 275 MiB after a 108292-token fill, just above the ~250 MiB knee where TG and PP collapse together; 3/3 byte-identical starts and TG recovered to 18.81 t/s after the deep fill, but there is little room for a heavier future build (b9672 once idled +545 MiB at an identical config). If that happens, q4_0 KV holds the same 131072 window at 720 MiB headroom for ~1% TG. The shipped DFlash drafter (dflash-kquant.gguf, --spec-type draft-dflash) is a LOSS here: it costs ~2.3 GiB, dropping TG 21.6 -> 15.3 and PP 425 -> 39 t/s at 21% acceptance -- it wants the 24 GB card the model card targets. UD-Q3_K_XL is the roomier alternative at 21.61 t/s TG / 2977 MiB headroom (ctx 81920, -ub 2048) if throughput matters more than quantization quality. reasoning_strength (low/medium/high/xhigh) is a chat-template kwarg; shipped at xhigh. high spends ~900 reasoning tokens on even a trivial question; xhigh can stall multi-call turns on the 16 GB box. See docs/BENCHMARKS.md (2026-08-10).
